Ich bin Ferdinand, habe in den letzten 10 Jahren 4 Unternehmen erfolgreich gegründet und dabei jedes Mal den Bereich Marketing & Growth verantwortet. Dabei habe ich viel richtig gemacht, einiges falsch, und vor allem eine Menge darüber gelernt, wie aus einem kleinen Startup ein gestandenes Unternehmen wird.
mieteinander ist meine neueste Gründung aus 2024. Den härtesten Weg - die ersten 2 Jahre seit dem Start bei Null- bin ich schon gegangen und weiß inzwischen, welche Kanäle bei uns funktionieren: Messen, Plattformintegrationen, Social Media, Webinare. Die nächste Phase ist jetzt die Skalierung dieser Kanäle. Dafür suche ich dich.
Wir würden eng zusammenarbeiten, und ich gebe gerne weiter, was ich in 10 Jahren gelernt habe. Was du hier vor allem bekommst, ist die Chance, etwas Eigenes entstehen zu sehen. Kampagnen, die du gebaut hast, Zahlen, die sich wegen dir bewegen und vor allem viele zwischenmenschliche Begegnungen- denn die Immobilienbranche ist ein People-Business.
Wer aus dem Marketing kommt, weiß, wie selten es ist, die eigenen Arbeitsergebnisse so klar zu sehen. Du bist kein kleines Rädchen in einem riesigen Uhrwerk, sondern sitzt selbst am Steuerhebel.
Was du mitbringen solltest: Lust, Dinge selbst anzupacken, ohne dass dir jemand jeden Schritt vorgibt. Wenn du das eher anstrengend findest, passen wir vermutlich nicht zusammen. Wenn es dich reizt, lies weiter.
Wir sind mieteinander – bundesweit spezialisiert auf die professionelle Optimierung von Mietverhältnissen in schlecht-vermieteten Wohnobjekten. Für Eigentümer holen wir aus bestehenden Beständen heraus, was möglich ist, ohne die Mieterseite zu vergessen. Unser Anspruch ist die faire Win-Win-Lösung: zufriedene Mieter, deutlich gesteigerte Objektwerte (im Schnitt 30–40 %) und ein Vergütungsmodell, das zu 100 % erfolgsbasiert ist.
Immer mehr Eigentümer geben ihre Objekte in unsere Hände, weil Mietverhandlungen Spezialwissen brauchen, das man sich intern nur schwer aufbaut. Wir übernehmen den kompletten Prozess – von der Potenzialanalyse über die Verhandlung bis zur digitalen Dokumentation.
Damit noch mehr Eigentümer von uns erfahren, suchen wir dich für unser Marketing in München.
Aufgaben
Du übernimmst nicht alles auf einmal. Wir starten mit den Kanälen, die schon laufen, und bauen Schritt für Schritt aus. Deine Schwerpunkte:
Events und Messen: Planung und Durchführung von rund drei Messen pro Jahr, von der Aussteller-Recherche über Berater-Briefings bis zur Koordinierung mit mir zusammen vor Ort.
Webinare: Eigene Webinare in festem Rhythmus aufsetzen und durchführen, inklusive Landing Page und Nachfass-Strecke. Dazu Partner-Webinare mit Finanzierungsvermittlern, Steuerberatern und Vermieter-Communities.
Partnernetzwerk und Tippgeber: Unser Netzwerk aus Steuerberatern, Finanzierungsvermittlern, Hausverwaltungen und Maklern ausbauen. Erstansprache, Onboarding und regelmäßiger Kontakt.
E-Mail-Marketing und Automation: Unseren Erfolgsfall-Newsletter in Newsletter-Tool betreuen und ausbauen, Segmentierung nach Lead-Status, automatisierte Nurture-Strecken (z. B. für Webinar-No-Shows).
Content und Sichtbarkeit: Referenzobjekte und Testimonials auf Website, Newsletter und Instagram ausspielen, unsere Instagram-Agentur steuern, Podcast-Gastauftritte und Fachartikel organisieren.
Reporting und Steuerung: Pipeline-Dashboard pflegen und die Kanäle monatlich über KPIs nachjustieren (Cost-per-Infogespräch, Lead-zu-Termin-Quote je Kanal).
Mittelfristig kommt ein größeres Projekt dazu: eine neue Tochtermarke von mieteinander aufbauen und launchen. Das ist Perspektive, kein Tag-eins-Auftrag.
Qualifikation
Berufserfahrung im Marketing, idealerweise B2B und gern in der Immobilien- oder Finanzbranche. Quereinstieg ist möglich, wenn der Rest passt.
Du arbeitest strukturiert und eigenständig und behältst mehrere Kanäle im Blick, ohne den Überblick zu verlieren. Du steuerst über KPIs, liest ein Dashboard und leitest daraus Entscheidungen ab, statt nach Bauchgefühl zu handeln.
Du arbeitest gern mit Menschen, ob am Messestand oder am Telefon mit potenziellen Multiplikatoren. Ein freundliches, verbindliches Auftreten gegenüber Partnern und Beratern gehört für dich dazu.
Erfahrung mit E-Mail-Marketing und gängigen Tools (MailerLite oder vergleichbar, CRM/HubSpot, Landing Pages, Social Media) ist ein Plus, aber kein Muss.

Du baust das operative Marketing mit auf und siehst direkt, was deine Arbeit bewirkt. Kurze Wege, direkte Zusammenarbeit mit der Geschäftsführung, schnelle Entscheidungen.
Gehalt : 50.000 bis 70.000 € je nach Erfahrung und ein leistungsbezogener Anteil, der mit unserem Wachstum mitzieht. Wir planen in Stufen und passen an, wenn die Zahlen stimmen.
Arbeitsweise : Flexible Arbeitszeiten, überwiegend Remote, da unser Team über Deutschland verteilt ist. Rund einen Tag pro Woche arbeitest du gemeinsame mit mir, einem der Gründer und CMO, in München, dazu mehrmals im Jahr Reisetätigkeit zu Messen und Beratertagen. Ein guter Mix aus Homeoffice, vor Ort und gemeinsamen Terminen.
Klingt nach dir? Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung – ein kurzes Anschreiben und dein Lebenslauf reichen uns. Wenn du Beispiele aus deinem bisherigen Marketing zeigen kannst, umso besser. Bei Fragen vorab kannst du dich jederzeit bei uns melden. Wir melden uns zeitnah zurück.

Growth Marketer heißt bei uns nicht "ein bisschen von allem".
Es heißt: Du treibst das Wachstum unserer Kunden über den Kanal, der es trägt - Meta Ads. Kein Kanal-Hopping, kein "wir machen jetzt auch TikTok". Wir sind eine Boutique-Agentur für hochpreisigen E-Commerce: Produkte ab mehreren hundert Euro AOV, erklärungsbedürftig, mit Kaufentscheidungen, die Wochen bis Monate dauern. In dieser Nische wollen wir die Besten in Deutschland sein. Dafür suchen wir Leute, die lieber eine Sache auf Weltklasse-Niveau machen als fünf Sachen auf LinkedIn-Niveau.
Zweiter Punkt, bevor du weiterliest: Wir arbeiten AI-nativ. Das schreibt inzwischen jede zweite Agentur, deshalb konkret: Wir bauen eigene AI-Werkzeuge. MCP-Anbindung an unsere Ad-Accounts, automatisierte Audits, Anomalie-Erkennung, eigene Skills für Angle- und Skript-Entwicklung. AI ist bei uns Standard-Werkzeug, nicht Notnagel.

Wer 2026 noch jede Analyse von Hand baut, ist uns zu langsam. Wer umgekehrt jede Entscheidung an die AI abgibt, liefert denselben Output wie jeder Wettbewerber mit demselben Modell. Wir suchen die Mitte: Du steuerst, AI beschleunigt.
Wenn dich beides anzieht - Fokus statt Bauchladen, AI als Hebel statt als Ersatz fürs Denken - lies weiter.
Wer wir sind: Divinely, eine Meta-Ads-Boutique für High-AOV E-Commerce mit bewusst kleinem Kundenportfolio. Unsere Kunden kaufen kein Button-Pushing, sondern Urteilsvermögen: dass wir ihr Geschäft verstehen - Marge, Customer Journey, Liquidität - und daraus die richtigen Wachstumsentscheidungen ableiten.

Das heißt auch: Bei uns sinkt manchmal der ROAS im Werbeanzeigenmanager, während das Geschäft des Kunden wächst. Und das ist dann genau richtig. Wer in Tages-ROAS denkt, wird bei uns unglücklich.
Aufgaben
Du führst das Wachstum deiner Accounts über Meta Ads - von Audit über Hypothese und Test-Roadmap bis Skalierung und Reporting. Strukturiert, nicht aus dem Bauch.
Du steuerst nach Total Business Numbers (Net Revenue, CAC, Deckungsbeitrag, MER) und inkrementellen KPIs, nicht nach Plattform-ROAS allein.
Du denkst über die Anzeige hinaus: Wenn der Wachstums-Bottleneck nicht in den Ads liegt (Offer, Landingpage, Produkt, Pricing), sagst du es dem Kunden klar und lieferst einen Alternativweg.
Du reverse-engineerst die Customer Journey hochpreisiger Produkte: Micro-Conversions als Algo-Futter, Post-Purchase-Surveys, Time-Lag-Messung.
Du baust deine Test-Roadmaps mit AI-Unterstützung. Unser Stack liefert dir Audits, Breakdowns und Anomalie-Signale; du lieferst die Hypothese und prüfst den Output, statt ihn blind zu übernehmen.
Du entwickelst Wachstums-Hypothesen (Segment → Mechanismus → fehlendes Set-Piece) und liest Creative-Performance jenseits der Vanity-Metriken.
Qualifikation

Du hast Meta Ads operativ und strategisch im Griff - Kampagnenarchitektur, Optimierungsziele, Creative-Testing - und kannst deine Entscheidungen einem Founder in Geschäftszahlen erklären.
Du denkst in Systemen: Hypothese → Test → Learning → nächster Test.
Du arbeitest täglich mit AI - eigene Prompts und Workflows, idealerweise schon mal Tool-Anbindungen oder Automatisierungen genutzt - und kannst konkret erzählen, wo AI dich schneller gemacht hat und wo du ihr bewusst nicht vertraust.
Du verstehst Inkrementalität (New-Customer-Steuerung) und warum Last-Click bei langen Journeys täuscht. Oder du willst genau das in den ersten 90 Tagen bei uns lernen und belegen.
Du bist konfrontationsfähig: Du nickst "morgen 5x skalieren" nicht ab, sondern führst den Kunden.

Ein Umfeld, in dem AI-Werkzeuge nicht beantragt, sondern gebaut werden.
Ein kleines, hochwertiges Kundenportfolio statt Fließband. Jede deiner Entscheidungen bewegt echtes Budget und echtes Geschäft.
Ein herausforderndes und anspruchsvolles Arbeitsumfeld, das stets im Wandel ist und deiner Arbeit Wertschätzung zollt.
Kompetitiver Gehalt basierend auf deiner Performance.
Eine lockere Atmosphäre mit flachen Hierarchien und jeder Menge Spaß, ohne dass die Professionalität verloren geht.
Arbeite so, wie du am produktivsten bist. Flexible Arbeitszeiten und Remote Work sind bei uns keine Fremdwörter.
Ausstattung mit den neusten Apple-Produkten.
Nette, professionelle und sorgfältig ausgesuchte Kunden - die dein Leben definitiv NICHT zur Hölle machen. Wir arbeiten mit unseren Kunden auf Augenhöhe.

Kurzbewerbung - Im Anschluss an die Profilsichtung: Ein paar Rückfragen per E-Mail oder Telefon.
2 x Gespräche - 1x mit Geschäftsführer & 1x mit einem Team-Member. Überprüfung der fachlichen und persönlichen Eignung.
Eine kompakte Probearbeit an einem realen Szenario. AI-Einsatz ist dabei ausdrücklich erlaubt und erwünscht - uns interessiert, wo du sie einsetzt und wo bewusst nicht.
Du erkennst dich wieder? Dann bewirb dich.

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

Gusto is looking for a seasoned performance marketer to own execution across paid social and emerging acquisition channels — testing new platforms, formats, and tactics to find what works before scaling. This is a high-visibility role at the intersection of performance marketing, channel experimentation, and AI-powered workflow design.

You will own execution and day-to-day strategy for paid social and new channel tests, working within Gusto's demand generation framework, with clear accountability to pipeline and revenue targets.

As a member of Gusto’s Demand Generation team, you will be embedded specifically within Paid Acquisition, a focused group responsible for driving awareness and pipeline through paid media. This team operates with high autonomy, a bias for experimentation, and a culture of cross-functional partnership. We hold ourselves to a high standard, move fast, and genuinely believe that being AI-native is part of what it means to do this job well today.

· Own paid social strategy and execution across Meta, LinkedIn, Reddit, Quora, and TikTok, driving full-funnel campaigns from brand awareness through retargeting and conversion, with accountability to pipeline and revenue targets.

· Manage significant, multi-million dollar budgets with rigor, including campaign pacing, forecasting, budget-vs-actuals analysis, and making the case for paid social investment in imperfect attribution environments.

· Apply and help refine Gusto's paid acquisition measurement framework, including attribution philosophy and budget allocation principles, in partnership with the broader marketing team.

· Lead creative strategy and testing at scale: briefing creative studios and agencies, structuring meaningful experiments, interpreting complex data sets to drive actionable insights, and building a clear learning roadmap.

· Serve as the team's go-to expert on paid social and AI-powered marketing workflows, documenting playbooks and best practices for the paid acquisition team.

· Identify, test, and validate new digital media channels and formats beyond core paid social — such as Google Demand Generation campaigns and ChatGPT ads — running structured pilots, defining success criteria upfront, and making the call on scale vs. kill within existing budget guardrails.

· Support new product launches by building and executing the paid acquisition plan for launch moments — channel mix, budget, creative, and timeline — in partnership with Integrated Marketing and Product Marketing.

· Partner with Web Marketing to align on landing page strategy, message match, and post-click conversion, because paid social performance doesn't end at the click.

· Use AI tools as a consistent, habitual part of your workflow: generating campaign briefs, developing copy variants, accelerating audience research, and building reusable systems that raise the bar for the whole team.

· Collaborate cross-functionally with Integrated Marketing, Communications, and Web to align paid social with integrated campaigns and earned media moments, and bring performance data back upstream to influence creative production and asset strategy.

· 7+ years of performance marketing experience at a B2B SaaS, performance marketing agency, or high-growth consumer organization, with deep expertise in paid social and a track record of testing and scaling new channels.

· Full-funnel ownership across two or more major paid social platforms (Meta, LinkedIn, Reddit, Quora, TikTok), including deep, hands-on, in-platform execution (campaign builds, audience/targeting strategy, creative testing, bid/budget management), with significant budget responsibility and a track record of driving measurable pipeline impact.

· Strong creative strategy and testing instincts: you know how to structure a test, distinguish a learning from a result, and translate performance data into creative direction.

· AI-fluent in practice, not just in theory; you use AI tools consistently in your day-to-day workflow to accelerate briefs, copy, and analysis, and have a track record of implementing AI-driven efficiencies for your team.

· Excellent cross-functional collaborator who can translate integrated briefs into paid social strategy, advocate for what the channel needs, and work effectively alongside brand, web, and comms partners.

· You are analytical and data-driven, with a clear point of view on attribution in imperfect measurement environments and comfort communicating paid social's contribution to business outcomes.

Our cash compensation amount for this role is $108,570/yr to $133,000/yr in Denver and $131,430/yr to $161,000/yr for San Francisco & New York. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate location, experience and expertise, and may vary from the amounts listed above.

Gusto has physical office spaces in Denver, San Francisco, and New York City. Employees who are based in those locations will be expected to work from the office on designated days approximately 2-3 days per week (or more depending on role). The same office expectations apply to all Symmetry roles, Gusto's subsidiary, whose physical office is in Scottsdale.

Note: The San Francisco office expectations encompass both the San Francisco and San Jose metro areas.

When approved to work from a location other than a Gusto office, a secure, reliable, and consistent internet connection is required. This includes non-office days for hybrid employees.

Our customers come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds, not just because it's the right thing to do, but because it makes our company stronger. If you share our values and our enthusiasm for small businesses, you will find a home at Gusto.

Gusto is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

Gusto considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. We want to see our candidates perform to the best of their ability.

Event Marketing Manager, 3P & Partner Events

As a key member of the Databricks Marketing team, you will design and execute high-impact third-party and partner events that accelerate pipeline, deepen customer relationships, and elevate the Databricks brand. In this role, you will translate business goals into an integrated event strategy, partnering closely with Sales, Product, and Marketing to deliver measurable outcomes. You will build repeatable programs and processes so our events scale efficiently as the business grows.

Outcomes

· Business impact (pipeline & revenue): Deliver an event portfolio that consistently meets or exceeds pipeline and revenue targets, with clear attribution, reporting, and optimization plans for each program that informs go-forward investment decisions.

· Audience growth & quality: Increase the volume and quality of target accounts and qualified leads across priority events, with a focus on high-intent engagement and conversion to pipeline.

· Brand & experience effectiveness: Deliver high-impact event experiences that clearly communicate company positioning and drive measurable engagement (e.g., session attendance, booth traffic, meetings, and activations tied to target personas).

· Integrated event strategy & execution: Transform priority events into fully integrated programs (booth, content, meetings and ancillary events) that present a unified narrative, improve lead quality and increase engagement across the event lifecycle.

· Program optimization & insights: Continuously improve event performance by applying insights from year-over-year data, attendee feedback, competitive analysis, and conversion metrics to inform planning and investment decisions toward the highest-yield programs.

· Sales & stakeholder alignment: Establish and scale a repeatable engagement model with Sales and cross-functional partners, resulting in strong pre-event planning, active in-event participation, and timely post-event follow-up, with measurable improvements in stakeholder satisfaction and pipeline conversion.

Competencies

· Proven event leadership experience owning end-to-end strategy and execution for complex, multi-stakeholder events that drive measurable pipeline and revenue outcomes.

· Strong command of event performance metrics, including how to set goals, forecast, and report on pipeline, lead quality, conversion, and ROI for executive and practitioner audiences.

· Demonstrated ability to partner closely with internal stakeholders, translating business priorities into event strategies and securing alignment on objectives, target accounts, follow-up plans, and success criteria.

· Experience optimizing budgets and resources, making data-informed tradeoffs while maintaining or elevating attendee experience.

· Exceptional program management and communication skills, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent events, navigate ambiguity, and influence cross-functional stakeholders at all levels.

· Deep customer and audience empathy, using insights from feedback, research, and data to continuously refine content, formats, and experiences to better serve target segments.

Hast Du noch Fragen? Wir stehen Dir gerne zur Verfügung. Schreib uns einfach an.

WRITER is the enterprise AI agent platform trusted by the marketing and sales teams behind the world’s biggest brands. In a world where every AI company sounds the same, WRITER is building something different. We believe a great brand doesn’t just look good. It earns trust, sharpens conviction, and gives people the confidence to act. We’re looking for someone who believes that just as deeply as we do.
Reporting into the VP of brand and communications, you’ll drive ownership of the WRITER brand, internal and external, from campaign strategy to the systems that make great brand work scalable. You’ll help shape how the world sees us, how our employees feel about us, how our product expresses us, and how AI makes all of that more powerful.

If you’re a brand leader who thinks in systems, ships with taste, and is genuinely excited about what agentic AI makes possible for marketing, this is your role.

Brand strategy and campaigns - You’ll lead brand campaign strategy from idea through activation — not just the brief, but the conviction behind it. You’ll develop concepts worth executing, manage the work end-to-end, and hold the bar for what “on-brand” actually means.

You’ll ensure every campaign builds something cumulative: a brand that people recognize, trust, and root for. You’ll partner closely with product marketing on integrated go-to-market campaigns, ensuring brand and demand work in lockstep.
The full customer and employee journey - Great brands don’t live in one channel. You’ll activate WRITER’s brand across the customer journey, and bring the same intentionality to the employee experience. Onboarding, all-hands, internal comms: the brand lives there too, and you’ll make sure it shows up with the same quality and care.
AI-native brand operations - WRITER brings the power of agentic marketing to the world’s best brands — and we run on our own platform.

You’ll own WRITER’s internal WRITER instance as the operational backbone of our brand: encoding our voice, guidelines, and creative standards into brand skills that the entire company relies on to produce high-quality, on-brand work at scale.

You’ll build and maintain the skill library that makes WRITER employees faster, sharper, and more consistent — without losing what makes us distinctively us. You’ll partner with product and engineering to translate that front-line experience into product insights, acting as an in-house advisor to make WRITER stronger for brand leaders everywhere.
Brand in the product - WRITER’s biggest brand touchpoint is the product itself. You’ll work with product and design to ensure our brand identity is felt inside the platform: in the copy, the experience, the moments that tell customers they’re working with something built with genuine craft and conviction.
Agency management - You’ll be WRITER’s day-to-day lead for our brand agency — setting the brief, driving the relationship, and making sure partners deliver work that actually moves us forward, giving them a clear point of view to work from.
Measurement and brand intelligence - What doesn’t get measured doesn’t get protected. You’ll define and own the metrics that matter — brand awareness, perception, campaign performance, pipeline influence — and use those signals to continuously sharpen strategy. You’ll conduct ongoing competitive and market research to keep WRITER’s brand ahead of the conversation, not just part of it.
Brand Central: the system behind the brand - You’ll build and own WRITER’s brand repository, creating a single, scalable source of truth for assets, guidelines, templates, and toolkits. Working hand-in-hand with the creative team, you’ll turn our brand into something the whole company can activate confidently without compromising consistency. You’ll also champion brand adoption across the organization, running enablement that makes internal teams genuine brand ambassadors.
⭐️ What you need
You’ve spent 7+ years building brands that stand for something, ideally at a high-growth B2B technology company where brand was a strategic imperative.
You’ve owned the strategy and the execution. You know the difference between a brand that looks good and a brand that creates belief, and you’ve built the latter.
You’re genuinely excited about agentic AI and its role in brand, and you bring a real point of view. You understand how AI can encode brand standards, scale creative output, and protect consistency without flattening distinctiveness. Ideally, you’ve worked with AI tools in a brand context and have opinions about what works and what doesn’t.
You’ve managed agencies well, which means you’ve written briefs that are actually useful and given feedback that makes work better instead of blander.
You’ve worked in or alongside product teams, and you understand how brand translates into product experiences. You’ve fought those fights and know how to win them.
You’ve built brand systems that scale — asset libraries, guidelines, repositories, brand skills or AI-powered toolkits — that genuinely help teams create on-brand work instead of just paying lip service to the guidelines.
You’re fluent in brand metrics. You know how to measure what matters, connect brand performance to business outcomes, and use data to defend and evolve strategy.
You communicate with precision and confidence. You can write a sharp brief, present a campaign with conviction, and tell a stakeholder why brand investment matters without resorting to platitudes.
You operate with low ego and high standards. You know how to build shared ownership and bring people along, because brand only works when the whole company believes in it.

At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale.
With $125M raised at Series B from IVP, Sequoia, Benchmark, CapitalG, and Sapphire Ventures, we’re at a stage where we’re continuing to develop new products, growth is accelerating, and all team members have meaningful impact on what we build and how we work together. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world.
Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement.

We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater.

We’re looking for a Product and Solutions Marketing Manager to help drive go-to-market for LangSmith Fleet and build the solutions marketing motion around enterprise AI adoption.
Fleet is LangChain’s product for bringing agents to every team in an organization. It enables anyone to build, use, and manage agents with natural language, while giving organizations the security, observability, and API extensibility they need to deploy agents across the business.
This role will help shape how we take Fleet to market across both sales-led and product-led growth motions. You’ll work on positioning and messaging, product launches, content, enablement, campaigns, customer storytelling, and cross-functional programs in partnership with product, sales, education, and marketing.
The audience is broad and nuanced: technical buyers who care about security, observability, integrations, APIs, and governance; technical champions who want to extend and operationalize agents; and nontechnical users who need to understand what agents can do for their day-to-day work. You’ll help translate a rapidly evolving product into clear stories, content, and programs that drive awareness, adoption, and revenue.
You’ll also help turn LangChain’s broader platform story into industry-specific solutions. That includes developing campaigns, collateral, and sales enablement for targeted enterprise segments such as financial services, healthcare, and life sciences. You’ll work closely with product, sales, demand generation, field marketing, education, and customer-facing teams to translate customer problems into clear narratives, programs, and assets that support pipeline and revenue.

Product marketing for Fleet
Help launch new Fleet capabilities in a fast-moving market. You’ll partner with product and GTM teams to bring new features and use cases to market.
Develop positioning and messaging for Fleet. You’ll help define how Fleet shows up across the website, sales materials, launch assets, campaigns, product pages, and customer-facing content.

Partner with demand generation on campaigns. You’ll help turn product narratives, use cases, launches, and customer insights into campaigns that drive pipeline and product adoption.

Solutions and enterprise marketing
Develop solution narratives for priority industries and enterprise use cases. Initial focus areas include financial services, healthcare, and life sciences, with room to expand based on GTM priorities.
Partner with demand generation, field marketing, and sales on integrated campaigns. You’ll create campaign materials and collateral for targeted enterprise motions. This may include solution briefs, industry landing page copy, campaign messaging, and webinar narratives.
Build sales enablement for enterprise conversations. You’ll create materials that help account teams explain LangChain’s value in regulated and complex environments, including industry talk tracks, use case maps, executive-ready decks, and objection handling.
Translate customer and field insights into repeatable sales plays. You’ll work with sales, solutions, and customer-facing teams to understand what resonates in the field and turn that into reusable messaging, collateral, and campaign programs.

You have current experience in product marketing, developer marketing, solutions marketing, enterprise marketing, or a related GTM role.
You’ve worked on technical products, developer tools, AI/ML products, B2B SaaS, infrastructure, automation, productivity tools, or platform products.
You can translate technical concepts into clear customer-facing messaging. You don’t need to be an engineer, but you should be comfortable learning technical products and asking good questions.
You’re excited by a product that serves multiple audiences: developers, technical buyers, operators, admins, and nontechnical end users.
You understand how sales-led and product-led motions can work together. You can create materials that help sales teams win while also helping self-serve users understand and adopt the product.
You understand enterprise marketing. You know how to create assets and campaigns for complex buying committees, regulated industries, and sales-led motions.
You write clearly and quickly. You can turn a product capability, customer problem, or technical workflow into useful content or enablement without a long ramp.
You like working cross-functionally. You’ll partner closely with product, sales, demand generation, field marketing, devrel, education, customer-facing teams, and the broader marketing team.
You’re comfortable with ambiguity and iteration. Fleet is evolving quickly, and the market for workplace agents is still being defined. You’re excited to ship, learn, and improve.
You have genuine curiosity about agents, enterprise AI adoption, and how they will change how teams work.
You use AI tools in your own work and are interested in finding new ways to increase your effectiveness with them.
Experience marketing developer tools, AI products, automation products, productivity tools, or enterprise SaaS platforms.
